newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Cuba protests over bid to search U.N. envoy's bags.
newsitem.headline: Cuba protests over bid to search U.N. envoy's bags.

text.p: Cuba protested to the United Nations on Friday that officials at New York's John F. Kennedy airport tried to search their U.N. envoy's luggage recently in a "gross violation" of diplomatic immunity.
Cuba said in a note circulated on Friday that the incident occurred as ambassador Bruno Rodriguez Parrilla was preparing to board a Northwest Airlines flight for Tokyo on August 17.

Although his bags were scanned by X-ray equipment which turned up no irregularities, airport officials and authorities, "exerting pressure and threatening to prohibit him from boarding, repeatedly tried to open and search the Cuban permanent representative's luggage," the note said.

The officials tried to justify the attempted search on the basis of general instructions issued by U.S. authorities, it added. The envoy was finally allowed to board 35 minutes after the flight was due to leave.

Cuba called it a "gross violation of the privileges and immunities granted to diplomatic personnel" under international agreements and an "attempt to enforce special, selective and discriminatory measures on a passenger merely on account of his status as a diplomat from the Republic of Cuba".

The note said that three days before the incident a Cuban U.N. diplomat advised U.S. officials of the ambassador's impending trip and of reports circulated at the United Nations "about flight security measures taken by United States authorities, such as the preparation of a list of countries allegedly linked to terrorism, whose nationals would be subject to special, discriminatory and selective measures at United States airports".
U.S. officials were said to have given assurances that diplomatic privileges and immunities would continue to be respected and that no further problems should arise.
